title: Normalization of a valuation ring and its prolongations
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finite algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $C=\{x\in L:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }V\}$ be the integral closure of $V$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $C$ is a nonzero integral domain integral over $V$, with fraction field $L$. Its set of maximal ideals is nonempty. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, the subring $C_{\mathfrak n}\subseteq L$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a valuation ring and $C_{\mathfrak n}\cap K=V$. Conversely, every valuation ring $W\subseteq L$ with $W\cap K=V$ is $C_{\mathfrak n}$ for a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$. No henselian, Noetherian, separability, rank, or module-finiteness assumption on $C/V$ is made.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1, converse proof, printed p. 11: 'F° is the integral closure of K° in F; it is semilocal with maximal ideals m_1,...,m_n and its localizations are the valuation rings of F extending K°' (used as standard background there). Full statement: Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra VI §8.6, Proposition 6 and its corollaries (WANTED). Local Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00IA (lemma-dominate) and Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal) give background only. Primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S2.SS2.

proof.text: Mathlib supplies the nonzero domain, integrality and fraction-field clauses for C by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal]. Nonemptiness of MaximalSpectrum C is the standard maximal ideal existence instance for any nontrivial commutative ring.

For x in L use [lem-trf-valuation-integral-multiplication-certificate] to obtain a,b,c,d in C with b=x*a, d=x*c, a-d=1. In D=C_n, either a or -d is a unit. In the first case x=b/a belongs to D; in the second x^-1=c/d belongs to D. Thus D is a valuation subring by [def-trf-valuation-ring]. The nonzero conditions needed for division follow by mapping units to L.

By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], n contracts to a maximal ideal of V, hence its unique maximal ideal. The localization unit test makes V map locally into D∩K. Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection] to get D∩K=V. This needs no choice of a dominating valuation ring.

For an extending valuation subring W, the containment direction of [lem-trf-integral-closure-valuation-intersection] puts C inside W. In Lean this direction is implemented using the already proved Mathlib valuation normality instance and Subring.integralClosure_le_iff, not the sorried Sheaf normality theorem. Let q be the contraction of its maximal ideal to C. For a in V, the criterion a∈nonunits iff a=0 or a^-1∉V, together with W∩K=V and preservation of inverses, identifies q∩V with the maximal ideal of V. Therefore q is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal].

Fractions embed D=C_q into W: denominators outside q are units of W. To reflect units, write y=r/s in D. If y is a unit of W, then r=y*s is a unit there, hence r∉q. The localization unit test makes y a unit of D too. Thus W dominates D. Since D is a valuation subring, maximality in the domination order, as used in [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection], forces W=D.

The localization criterion IsUnit(c/1) iff c∉n recovers n from D as an embedded subring of L. An equality of two embedded localizations gives a ring equivalence preserving c/1, so these unit tests give equality of ideals. This proves uniqueness.

Steps: (1) integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal with P=V gives a domain, integral, normal, Frac=L. (2) Lying-over plus prime-over-maximal gives nonemptiness; going-up from n∩V⊆m with maximality of n gives n∩V=m. (3) The localization-normal-domain and nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates nodes give U; nagata-valuation-intersection gives U∩K=V. (4)-(6) I checked by hand the coefficient normalization, the tail identities c_i=-Σ_{j≤i}a_jx^{j-i-1} and xc_i=-Σ_{j≤i}a_jx^{j-i}, and the cases k=0, k=r and 0<k<r (c_{k-1}-xc_k=1, unit dichotomy in local D). The new leaf puts c_i and xc_i in C. (7) inverse-maximal-ideal gives C_n=U. (8) valuation-ring-normal gives C⊆W; q=m_W∩C lies over m, is maximal, and C_q⊆W is dominated, so W=C_q. (9) n is the contraction of the nonunits of C_n, giving uniqueness. lean.statement: theorem integralClosure_maximal_localizations (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] (V : ValuationSubring K) : Nontrivial (integralClosure V L) ∧ IsDomain (integralClosure V L) ∧ Algebra.IsIntegral V (integralClosure V L) ∧ IsFractionRing (integralClosure V L) L ∧ Nonempty (MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure V L)) ∧ (∀ n : MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure V L), ∃ W : ValuationSubring L, W.toSubring = (@Localization.subalgebra.ofField (integralClosure V L) L _ n.asIdeal.primeCompl n.asIdeal.primeCompl_le_nonZeroDivisors _ _ (integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_finite_extension K L)).toSubring ∧ W.comap (algebraMap K L) = V) ∧ (∀ W : ValuationSubring L, W.comap (algebraMap K L) = V → ∃! n : MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure V L), W.toSubring = (@Localization.subalgebra.ofField (integralClosure V L) L _ n.asIdeal.primeCompl n.asIdeal.primeCompl_le_nonZeroDivisors _ _ (integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_finite_extension K L)).toSubring)
